addresses.help:
Who answers for one requirement, and which document says so.

The assessor's direction of travel. Name any requirement - NIST, HIPAA,
HITRUST - and this resolves it through the crosswalk to the topics the
registry anchors, then names the owner and the pages.

Every claim says how it was reached: anchored directly, inherited from a
parent control, or reached through a published crosswalk. The last is
the weakest and is labelled as such, because a mapping is not evidence
that anybody wrote the requirement down.
addresses.name: addresses

params.help: Topic registry (default: config/topics.yaml).
params.name: topics_path

params.help: Path to a controls.json. Repeatable - pass the framework the requirement belongs to as well as the NIST catalog.
params.name: controls_paths

boundary.help:
Show what may be sent to the configured model, and why.

Providers are classified by where the bytes end up - local, self-hosted,
or a third-party processor - and content by who may hold it. The table is
the pairing between them, and it is checked before a call rather than
described in a README.

Run it to answer "can this configuration work offline" without having to
remember, and to see a refusal's reasoning before a command hits it.
boundary.name: boundary

params.help: Classify these files or directories too, and say whether the configured provider may receive them. Repeatable.
params.name: paths

bundle.help:
Everything one team answers for: topics, requirements, documents, cadence.

The question a team lead asks, which `coverage` answers only by being
read whole and filtered by eye. Set arithmetic over the registry - no
model involved, and the answer is exactly as good as the registry is.
bundle.name: bundle

params.help: Topic registry (default: config/topics.yaml).
params.name: topics_path

params.help: Path to a controls.json. Repeatable.
params.name: controls_paths

check.help:
Check the content tree before anything is published.

Entirely offline, so it runs on a pull request from a fork with no
credentials - which is where you want it. Catches the mistakes that
survive review and fail later: two files claiming one Confluence page,
a link to a document somebody renamed, a rewrite that dropped the
framework citations a document exists to carry.
check.name: check

params.help: Markdown content tree to check. Defaults to `zardoz.content_dir`, else docs/.
params.name: content_dir

params.help: Where the synthesis files live, for the dropped-citation check. Skipped if the directory isn't there.
params.name: synthesis_dir

params.help: Treat warnings as failures too. For a repo that has finished migrating.
params.name: strict

coverage.help:
Report which in-scope controls no topic owns, and which two topics claim.

Orphaned controls mean nobody is doing the work. Contested controls are
worse: it looks covered while each owner assumes the other has it. Both
are pure set arithmetic over the topic registry - no LLM involved. See
README's "One topic, one team".
coverage.name: coverage

params.help: Topic registry (default: config/topics.yaml). Copy config/topics.example.yaml to start.
params.name: topics_path

params.help: Path to a controls.json. Repeatable - pass the NIST 800-53 file plus any other framework you want reachability reported for.
params.name: controls_paths

params.help: Limit the scope to one NIST baseline. 'Orphaned' only means anything relative to a defined scope, so this is usually what you want.
params.name: baseline

params.help: List every orphaned control, not just the first 40.
params.name: show_all

params.help: Exit non-zero if anything is orphaned, contested, or anchored to an unknown control - for use as a CI gate.
params.name: strict

params.help: Emit the report as JSON instead of a text summary.
params.name: as_json

check.help: Report what in each overlay no longer matches the catalogs.
check.name: check

params.help: A controls.json. Repeatable; pass the 800-53 catalog and the mapped framework's.
params.name: controls_paths

params.help: Directory of overlays (default: config/crosswalks).
params.name: overlay_dir

params.help: Exit non-zero when anything needs attention.
params.name: strict

propose.help:
Ask the configured model to read each requirement against 800-53.

One call per requirement. Nothing it says is a decision: a published
pair it confirms gains the quotes that justify it, one it could not
justify is flagged but stays accepted, and a pair it adds is proposed.
Run `policyforge crosswalk review` to decide them.
propose.name: propose

params.help: A controls.json. Repeatable; pass the 800-53 catalog and the mapped framework's.
params.name: controls_paths

params.help: The overlay to record proposals in (default: config/crosswalks/<framework>.yaml; seeded from the published mapping when it does not exist).
params.name: overlay

params.help: Propose for this requirement id only. Repeatable.
params.name: only

review.help:
Decide, one at a time, each pair a model flagged or proposed.

Flagged published pairs come first (the ones a model could not find a
basis for), then new proposals. Each decision is written as it is made,
with who made it and when. Accept keeps or adds the pair; reject removes
it from everything built on this crosswalk.
review.name: review

params.help: A controls.json. Repeatable; pass the 800-53 catalog and the mapped framework's.
params.name: controls_paths

params.help: Recorded as the reviewer (default: git user.name).
params.name: who

seed.help:
Write an overlay holding the published mapping, every pair accepted.

Changes nothing on its own: the pipeline reads the same pairs it did
before. It is the file you then review: reject a pair by changing its
status, add one with a new row, and record why.
seed.name: seed

params.help: The framework to map, as its catalog names it.
params.name: framework

params.help: A controls.json. Repeatable; pass the 800-53 catalog and the mapped framework's.
params.name: controls_paths

params.help: Where to write the overlay (default: config/crosswalks/<framework>.yaml).
params.name: out

params.help: Overwrite an existing overlay.
params.name: force

crosswalk.help:
Your organization's reviewed mapping of a framework onto 800-53.

Published crosswalks are pairs with no stated relationship or reasoning.
An overlay in config/crosswalks/ records which pairs your organization
accepts, rejects or has added, and only accepted pairs reach `map`,
`synthesize`, `coverage`, `bundle` and Zardoz.
crosswalk.name: crosswalk

drift.help:
Report what a framework update changed, and what it reaches.

A catalog bump touches a few dozen controls out of a thousand, and behind
those sit a handful of your topics and a smaller handful of your
documents. Everything else is unaffected and should stay unread.

Run the ETL, then run this - the ETL overwrites the catalog in place and
git is still holding the version you had, so no snapshot is needed:

    policyforge etl-oscal
    policyforge drift --controls data/frameworks/nist-800-53-r5/controls.json
drift.name: drift

params.help: The updated catalog. Compared against its committed version unless --old says otherwise.
params.name: controls_path

params.help: Explicit previous catalog. Without it, the version git has.
params.name: old_path

params.help: Git revision to compare against when --old is not given.
params.name: revision

params.help: Registry, to say which topics a change reaches.
params.name: topics_path

params.help: Content tree, to say which documents cite a changed control.
params.name: content_dir

params.help: Ledger, to say which recorded decisions a change reaches.
params.name: parameters_path

params.help: Show the changed lines of each control statement.
params.name: detail

params.help: Exit non-zero when anything substantive changed. For a scheduled job that should open an issue rather than pass quietly.
params.name: fail_on_change

edit-confluence.help:
Edit one live Confluence page from a plain-language instruction.

Fetches the page, plans the edits, shows you the plan and the resulting
diff, and publishes only if you pass --apply and confirm. The page's
"before" state is recorded to local version history either way, and the
plan is saved alongside the revision, so there is always something to
diff against and a record of why it changed.
edit-confluence.name: edit-confluence

params.help: What to change, in plain language.
params.name: instruction

params.help: Confluence space key.
params.name: space

params.help: Exact page title to edit.
params.name: title

params.help: Confluence base URL, e.g. https://x.atlassian.net/wiki.
params.name: host

params.help: Which document tier this page is. Tells the planner what altitude to edit at - a threshold change belongs in a Standard, not a Policy.
params.name: tier

params.help: Actually publish the edit. Without this the command plans, rewrites and shows you the diff, but changes nothing in Confluence.
params.name: do_apply

params.help: Skip the confirmation prompt before publishing.
params.name: yes

params.help: Proceed even though the page uses Confluence macros this tool cannot round-trip. They will be degraded or lost. Read the warning first.
params.name: allow_macros

params.help: Proceed even though the page contains text addressed to the reader of a prompt rather than to the organization. Look at the page first.
params.name: allow_reader_directed

params.help: Where the revised markdown and its plan are written.
params.name: out_dir

params.help: Where local version history is recorded (default: output/.history).
params.name: history_dir

edit-topic.help:
Apply one instruction across a topic's whole document set.

A change like "access reviews move to monthly" lands differently in each
tier: the Standard states the requirement, the Procedure carries the
steps, and the Policy usually shouldn't change at all. Each page is
planned separately and tier-aware, but reviewed and published as one
change - and a page whose plan comes back empty is left alone rather than
having an edit forced into it.
edit-topic.name: edit-topic

params.help: What to change, in plain language.
params.name: instruction

params.help: Topic in the registry whose documents to edit.
params.name: topic_name

params.help: Topic registry to resolve --topic-name against.
params.name: topics_path

params.help: Confluence base URL, e.g. https://x.atlassian.net/wiki. Edits the live pages. Give this or --content-dir, not both.
params.name: host

params.help: Edit the topic's markdown files in this content tree instead of the live pages, so the change is reviewed as a pull request and published on merge. Give this or --host, not both.
params.name: content_dir

params.help: Comma-separated subset of tiers to edit (e.g. 'standard,procedure'). Default: every page the topic declares.
params.name: tiers

params.help: Actually publish. Without this nothing in Confluence changes.
params.name: do_apply

params.help: Skip the confirmation prompt before publishing.
params.name: yes

params.help: Proceed even though a page uses Confluence macros this tool cannot round-trip.
params.name: allow_macros

params.help: Proceed even though a page contains text addressed to the reader of a prompt rather than to the organization. Look at the page first.
params.name: allow_reader_directed

params.help: Where revised markdown and plans are written.
params.name: out_dir

params.help: Where local version history is recorded (default: output/.history).
params.name: history_dir

etl-arc-ampe.help:
Fetch CMS's ARC-AMPE Volume II baseline and parse it into this schema.

Public domain - published by CMS, a federal agency, with no copyright
notice or redistribution restriction, same basis as the NIST and eCFR
sources.

Note which volume this reads. Volume I is the narrative PDF and holds no
controls; Volume II is the System Security and Privacy Plan workbook,
and its `AE Mandatory Baseline` sheet is the catalog - 402 controls
required of an ACA Administering Entity, with CMS's parameter decisions
already written into the control text. The sheet is found by its shape
rather than its name, so the Direct Enrollment Entity workbook reads the
same way via --export. See ingest/arc_ampe.py.
etl-arc-ampe.name: etl-arc-ampe

params.help: Read a local ARC-AMPE Volume II workbook instead of fetching CMS's. Use this for the Direct Enrollment Entity baseline, which CMS distributes through zONE rather than publishing.
params.name: export_path

params.help: Document version to stamp, e.g. "v1.02". Default: the version this loader is pinned to.
params.name: version

params.help: The 800-53 catalog to crosswalk against. ARC-AMPE numbers its controls with 800-53 identifiers, so each one that resolves here is anchored on its equivalent. If absent, prints a notice and carries on without a crosswalk - the catalog is usable alone, just invisible to `policyforge map`.
params.name: nist_path

params.help: Where to write the parsed control data.
params.name: out

etl-fedramp.help:
Fetch FedRAMP's published control tailoring and apply it to 800-53.

Public domain - a US federal program, same basis as the NIST and eCFR
sources. Read from `fedramp-consolidated-rules.json` in `FedRAMP/rules`,
which that repository calls its canonical rules dataset.

This writes a profile, not a baseline. FedRAMP's machine-readable
Low/Moderate/High baseline selection used to live in
`GSA/fedramp-automation`, and that repository no longer exists - so
nothing here says which controls a given system must implement, and
`Control.baseline` is deliberately left unset rather than guessed. What
it does carry is FedRAMP's own two additions to the controls it does
speak to: the organization-defined values FedRAMP has already decided,
and the guidance it layers on top. See ingest/fedramp.py.
etl-fedramp.name: etl-fedramp

params.help: The 800-53 catalog this tailoring is applied to. Produced by `policyforge etl-oscal`.
params.name: nist_path

params.help: Where to write the parsed control data.
params.name: out

etl-govramp.help:
Parse your own GovRAMP controls matrix into this project's schema.

GovRAMP's Terms & Conditions claim ownership of the documents published
on their site, and no redistribution grant was found - so, like HITRUST,
this project never bundles the matrix and never fetches it. You supply
the workbook and it is parsed locally, in memory. Nothing is written
unless you pass --out.

Pass the workbook as GovRAMP publishes it rather than an extract of it:
the controls sheet is found among the template's other thirteen by its
header captions, so the Low, Moderate and High workbooks all read
without being told which they are.

What this gives you that the 800-53 catalog does not is the profile's
own two additions - the parameter values GovRAMP has already decided
("at least every 3 years"), which `policyforge parameters` would
otherwise leave open for you to answer, and the requirements it layers
on top of a control - across the Core/Ready/Authorized tiers. Those
tiers are *not* impact levels: one Moderate matrix holds all three, and
60 of its 319 controls stand between a service offering and Core.

See ingest/govramp.py for the framework's structure and
ingest/govramp_export.py for how the sheet and its two-row header are
found. If detection fails on your workbook, `policyforge generate-parser
--framework govramp` drafts a loader for it from a sample.
etl-govramp.name: etl-govramp

params.help: Your own GovRAMP controls matrix workbook (.xlsx/.xlsm), as published. Keep it in local_content/, which is gitignored.
params.name: export_path

params.help: FIPS 199 level this matrix is for. Default: read from the workbook's cover sheet, then from the filename. Worth setting on a template somebody has been working in, where the cover sheet is the first thing edited.
params.name: impact_level

params.help: Revision and template version to stamp, e.g. "Rev 5 (V1.06)". Default: the revision from the cover sheet plus the version in the filename.
params.name: version

params.help: Write the parsed catalog here as controls.json. Omit to parse and report without writing anything, which is the safe default for licensed content.
params.name: out

params.help: Write --out even though this repository has not declared `frameworks.allow_licensed_in_repo`.
params.name: force

etl-hipaa.help:
Fetch the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR 164 Subpart C) from eCFR's public
API and parse it into this project's data schema. Public domain - a US
federal regulation, same basis as NIST/FedRAMP/ARC-AMPE - so unlike
HITRUST/GovRAMP this is safe to bundle directly. See
ingest/hipaa_loader.py for parsing details.
etl-hipaa.name: etl-hipaa

params.help: Specific eCFR effective date (YYYY-MM-DD) to fetch, for reproducibility. Default: eCFR's current published date for Title 45.
params.name: date

params.help: Where to write the parsed control data.
params.name: out

etl-hipaa-crosswalk.help:
Attach NIST's official HIPAA-Security-Rule-to-SP-800-53-Rev-5 crosswalk
to the HIPAA control data, so `map`/`synthesize` can pull HIPAA
requirements into a NIST-anchored topic.

Source is NIST's Cybersecurity and Privacy Reference Tool (CPRT), not SP
800-66r2's PDF - Appendix D of that document states the mapping table was
removed from the PDF and published in CPRT instead. See
ingest/hipaa_crosswalk_loader.py.
etl-hipaa-crosswalk.name: etl-hipaa-crosswalk

params.help: HIPAA controls.json produced by `etl-hipaa`, to enrich in place.
params.name: controls_path

params.help: Parse this saved CPRT payload instead of fetching (e.g. tests/fixtures/cprt_hipaa_to_800-53r5.json). Offline/reproducible.
params.name: fixture_path

params.help: Where to write the enriched data (default: overwrite --controls).
params.name: out

etl-hitrust.help:
Parse your own licensed HITRUST CSF export into this project's schema.

HITRUST CSF is licensed content. This project never bundles it and never
fetches it: you supply an export from your own MyCSF licence and it is
parsed locally, in memory. Nothing is written unless you pass --out.

Prefer a CSV export where you have the choice. The rendered HTML/MHTML of
the same report is more clearly labelled but carries markedly fewer
authoritative-source mappings, which is most of what makes a CSF export
worth ingesting.

See ingest/hitrust.py for the framework's structure and
ingest/hitrust_export.py for how the columns are identified. If detection
fails on your export, `policyforge generate-parser --framework hitrust`
drafts a loader for it from a sample.
etl-hitrust.name: etl-hitrust

params.help: Your own MyCSF/HITRUST CSF export (.csv, .tsv, .xlsx, .html, .mhtml). Keep it in local_content/, which is gitignored.
params.name: export_path

params.help: CSF release this export is of, e.g. "v11.7". Default: read from the filename if it names one - a MyCSF export states its release nowhere inside.
params.name: version

params.help: Write the parsed catalog here as controls.json. Omit to parse and report without writing anything, which is the safe default for licensed content.
params.name: out

params.help: Write --out even though this repository has not declared `frameworks.allow_licensed_in_repo`.
params.name: force

etl-oscal.help:
Fetch NIST's official OSCAL edition of SP 800-53 Rev 5 (plus the
Low/Moderate/High baseline profiles) and parse it into this project's
data schema.

Public domain - a US government work, same basis as the eCFR and CPRT
sources. Unlike `etl-vault`, this needs no pre-existing vault, so it's
the way to populate 800-53 data from scratch. See ingest/oscal_loader.py.
etl-oscal.name: etl-oscal

params.help: Where to write the parsed control data.
params.name: out

params.help: Skip fetching the Low/Moderate/High profiles (controls load without baseline tagging, which `ssp --baseline` needs).
params.name: no_baselines

etl-vault.help:
Parse NIST 800-53 control notes from an existing vault into this
project's data schema. Public-domain content only - see
ingest/nist_vault_loader.py for what crosswalk columns are stripped
by default and why.
etl-vault.name: etl-vault

params.help: Path to an Obsidian vault's Frameworks/NIST-800-53/Controls/ directory.
params.name: controls_dir

params.help: Where to write the parsed, public-domain-only control data.
params.name: out

export-confluence.help: Convert a generated markdown document to Confluence storage format and publish it.
export-confluence.name: export-confluence

params.help: Path to a generated markdown document (from `policyforge generate`).
params.name: doc_path

params.help: Confluence space key to publish into.
params.name: space

params.help: Page title.
params.name: title

params.help: Confluence base URL, e.g. https://yourorg.atlassian.net/wiki.
params.name: host

params.help: Parent page ID, if nesting under an existing page.
params.name: parent_id

params.help: Print the converted Confluence storage format instead of publishing.
params.name: dry_run

frameworks.help:
List the framework catalogs on disk, and their licence position.

A catalog is public domain or it is licensed, and that decides which
repository may hold a copy of it. This repository may hold only the
former; your own private repository can very often hold both, because
your MyCSF or GovRAMP licence permits internal use.

Licensed content committed to a repository that has not declared the
right to hold it is reported as an error - set
`frameworks.allow_licensed_in_repo: true` in config.yaml if your licence
permits yours to carry it.
frameworks.name: frameworks

generate.help: Draft a Standard, Policy, or Procedure document from a synthesized topic.
generate.name: generate

params.help: Document tier to draft. 'policy' and 'procedure' require --standard, so they can reference the Standard document by name.
params.name: tier

params.help: Path to a synthesized topic markdown file produced by `policyforge synthesize`.
params.name: synthesis_path

params.help: Path to the already-generated Standard document this Policy or Procedure implements. Required when --tier policy or --tier procedure.
params.name: standard_path

params.help: Where to write the drafted document (default: output/<tier>s/<synthesis-filename>).
params.name: out

params.help: Where local version history is recorded (default: output/.history). See `policyforge history`.
params.name: history_dir

generate-parser.help:
Generate a deterministic ETL parser for a BYOC framework export via your
configured LLM, from a real sample export file.

The sample is part of the prompt, so the code that comes back was written
under the influence of a file this tool did not write - and it is about
to run over a licensed one. So it is checked before it runs, run once
under watch, and kept out of the package until you promote it. Nothing
under ingest/*_loader.py calls the LLM at parse time - only this command
does, and only when you run it.
generate-parser.name: generate-parser

params.help: Which BYOC framework this sample export is for.
params.name: framework

params.help: Path to a real sample export from your own license (e.g. a MyCSF CSV/Excel export). Its full content is sent to your configured LLM provider - confirm your license terms permit that before running this.
params.name: sample_path

params.help: Where to write the candidate parser (default: output/parsers/<framework>_loader.py). It is checked and trial-run there, and not imported by anything until promoted.
params.name: out

params.help: Overwrite --out, or the promoted module, if it exists.
params.name: force

params.help: Skip the confirmation prompt before sending --sample's content to the LLM provider.
params.name: yes

params.help: Copy the candidate into src/policyforge/ingest/ once it passes the static check and its trial run returns records. Without this it stays in output/ for review.
params.name: promote

history.help: List (or diff) the locally recorded version history for one document.
history.name: history

params.help: Document slug/filename stem - the stem of the file `policyforge generate` wrote via --out (e.g. 'authenticator-mgmt' for authenticator-mgmt.md), the --name given to `import-confluence`, or for --tier confluence, the page title slugified (e.g. 'access-control-standard').
params.name: name

params.help: Where local version history is recorded (default: output/.history).
params.name: history_dir

params.help: Show a unified diff between two versions instead of listing them: 'N:M' for specific version numbers (e.g. '2:3'), or 'latest' for the two most recent versions.
params.name: diff_range

import-confluence.help:
Pull a page's current content back out of Confluence, converting it to
markdown, and record it into the same local version-history stream
`generate` uses for --tier/--name - so you can diff what this tool last
generated against what's actually live (e.g. after a manual edit).
import-confluence.name: import-confluence

params.help: Which document tier this Confluence page corresponds to - determines which local version-history stream the import is recorded into.
params.name: tier

params.help: Document slug/filename stem, matching what `policyforge generate` used, e.g. 'authenticator-mgmt'. Determines the version-history stream and the default --out path.
params.name: name

params.help: Confluence space key to read from.
params.name: space

params.help: Page title to look up.
params.name: title

params.help: Confluence base URL, e.g. https://yourorg.atlassian.net/wiki.
params.name: host

params.help: Where to write the imported markdown (default: output/<tier>s/<name>.imported.md - deliberately not the same filename `generate` writes, so an import never silently overwrites a fresh draft).
params.name: out

params.help: Where local version history is recorded (default: output/.history).
params.name: history_dir

init.help:
Lay out a PolicyForge project: bundled catalogs, example configs, .gitignore.

Every command reads `config/` and `data/frameworks/` relative to where it
runs. A clone of the repository already has them; an installed package
(Homebrew, pipx, pip) does not, and this writes them. The public-domain
catalogs are copied in - NIST 800-53, FedRAMP, ARC-AMPE, the HIPAA
Security Rule - with a README for each bring-your-own one.

Never overwrites: a file that already exists is kept, so running it again,
or inside a clone, changes nothing you have edited.
init.name: init

llm-check.help: Confirm your configured API key + model actually work.
llm-check.name: llm-check

params.help: Path to a controls.json. Repeatable, and normally repeated: a cross-framework crosswalk needs every framework loaded together, so passing only the NIST file produces a crosswalk with nothing to cross-reference.
params.name: controls_paths

params.help: Where to write the built crosswalk.
params.name: out

mcp.help:
Serve the read-only analyses as MCP tools over stdio.

Lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any MCP client ask this repository
which controls nobody owns, what a team is accountable for, or where a
HIPAA citation is addressed - with the content boundary, the ledger and
the citation checks all still in the path, because the answers come from
the same functions the CLI calls.

Read-only, structurally: a test walks this package's AST and fails if any
module so much as names the publish path. Editing a live policy page
stays here in the CLI, behind its dry run, macro check, version guard and
explicit confirmation.

This speaks stdio and is spawned by a client; it binds no port. Configure
it as a command, not a URL.
mcp.name: mcp

params.help: Synced document snapshot (default: the same one `zardoz` uses).
params.name: corpus_dir

params.help: Topic registry (default: config/topics.yaml).
params.name: topics_path

model-log.help:
What was sent to which model, when, and at what cost.

Every model call this tool makes is recorded - provider, model, the
document or control it was about, token counts, cost, and a hash of the
prompt. Not the prompt and not the reply: a record that quoted what it
saw would copy licensed content into a file, which is the leak it exists
to disprove.

This is the answer to "which documents did that model touch", asked the
day a model turns out to have been weakening the requirements it cited.
model-log.name: model-log

params.help: What to group the totals by.
params.name: by

params.help: Only calls about this document or control.
params.name: subject

params.help: Only calls answered by this model.
params.name: model_filter

params.help: Only calls on or after this ISO date, e.g. 2026-09-01.
params.name: since

params.help: Ledger to read. Defaults to `llm.ledger.path`, else output/.model-log/calls.jsonl.
params.name: ledger_file

parameters.help:
Record one decided value per organization-defined parameter.

SP 800-53 does not say how often to review accounts - it says
[Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and leaves it to you, 1,210
times across the catalog. Today those get decided implicitly inside
generated prose, by a model with no memory of what it chose for the
neighbouring control, so the Access Control Standard says quarterly and
the SSP says annually and nobody decided anything.

A value recorded here is substituted into the control text before
synthesis, so every document drawn from that control agrees, and the
reasoning stays next to the value where an assessor can find it.
parameters.name: parameters

params.help: Framework controls.json to read parameters from. Repeatable.
params.name: controls_paths

publish.help:
Publish the content tree to the pages its frontmatter declares.

Each document names its own destination, so the file-to-page mapping
lives in the repository under review rather than in a workflow argument.
A document with no `confluence:` block is not published, which is how a
draft stays a draft.

A page somebody edited on the wiki since this tool last wrote it is not
overwritten: it is reported as moved and the run exits non-zero, so a CI
job fails where it would otherwise have destroyed the edit in silence.

Plans by default and writes nothing; pass --apply once you have read it.
publish.name: publish

params.help: Markdown content tree to publish from.
params.name: content_dir

params.help: Confluence base URL. Defaults to `zardoz.host`.
params.name: host

params.help: Which store to publish to. Defaults to `publish.target`, else confluence.
params.name: target

params.help: GitHub wiki repository as owner/name. Defaults to `publish.github_wiki.repository`.
params.name: repository

params.help: Name of the environment variable holding the GitHub token. Defaults to `publish.github_wiki.token_env`; without either, git uses your credential helper.
params.name: token_env

params.help: Publish to a wiki that is public, or whose visibility could not be determined. Licensed catalog content is never published to a public wiki whether or not this is passed.
params.name: allow_public

params.help: Only publish documents whose path contains this substring, so a CI job can republish just what a merge touched.
params.name: only

params.help: Actually publish. Without it, plan only.
params.name: apply_

params.help: Publish over pages using macros this tool cannot round-trip. This flattens them; do not pass it to get past a skip you haven't read.
params.name: allow_macros

params.help: Overwrite pages changed on the wiki since this tool last wrote them. That destroys the change; pull it and review instead unless you have decided otherwise.
params.name: force

pull.help:
Bring live Confluence pages down into the tree as markdown.

The way back. Somebody will edit the wiki directly - that is what a wiki
is for - and without this, every such edit is either lost on the next
publish or quietly makes the repo wrong. Pulling turns it into a diff on
a branch.

Pages using macros this tool cannot round-trip are refused rather than
written, because the file would look correct and destroy them on the
first publish.
pull.name: pull

params.name: content_dir

params.name: host

params.name: tier

params.name: allow_macros

roles.help:
List the tool and team roles config can assign.

These keys go under `org.vendors` and `org.teams` in config.yaml, and
naming a role is what makes substitution deterministic: the generator is
told what a tool is *for* rather than inferring it from a product name,
and every placeholder for a filled role is then replaced exactly.

The lists are not exhaustive. They cover what NIST 800-53 and HIPAA
Security Rule procedures actually reference; a tool fitting none of them
can still be passed as a plain list.
roles.name: roles

params.help: Which taxonomy to list.
params.name: kind

satisfies.help:
What a published document can be shown against, and how strong the evidence is.

The assessor's direction of travel, from the page rather than the
requirement: name a document and this reports the requirements it cites,
the ones those citations reach through the crosswalk, and - separately -
the controls its topic claims that nothing in the topic actually says.

The citations in the text are the evidence. A topic anchor is an
intention, so the two are never added together. Every crosswalked
mapping says where it came from: the published crosswalk, an overlay row
somebody reviewed, or an overlay row nobody has. The last are shown and
marked rather than dropped. No model call and no network.

Two resolution rules worth knowing, because the counts look wrong
without them. Citing an enhancement counts as citing its control, so a
topic that cites AC-2(3) is not reported as never mentioning AC-2 - the
same reading `coverage` and `drift` use. And a topic's anchors are
answered by its documents together rather than one file at a time, so a
Policy is not reported as missing anchors its own Procedure cites; the
report names how much it searched. Under --document, one file is all
there is to search, and it says so.
satisfies.name: satisfies

params.help: Path to a controls.json. Repeatable - pass the NIST catalog plus every framework you want the documents resolved against.
params.name: controls_paths

params.help: Exit non-zero if any document cites a requirement no loaded catalog has. A citation pointing nowhere is a defect in the document, so this is the CI gate.
params.name: strict

params.help: Also exit non-zero if any mapping rests on an overlay entry nobody has reviewed. Separate from --strict: unreviewed is a state of the programme, not an error in the document.
params.name: require_reviewed

params.name: as_json

ssp.help:
Build a NIST 800-53 System Security Plan as a spreadsheet workbook.

Writes .xlsx - an open ISO standard that LibreOffice Calc opens and edits
natively, so no Excel licence is needed. Control text is copied verbatim
from the catalog; only the implementation narratives are LLM-drafted, and
those are marked as drafts requiring review. See ssp/workbook.py.
ssp.name: ssp

params.help: Path to a controls.json. Repeatable - pass the NIST 800-53 file plus any other framework whose mappings you want shown as crosswalk columns.
params.name: controls_paths

params.name: baseline

params.name: batch

params.name: out

synthesize.help:
Merge/dedupe controls for one topic into synthesized requirement prose.

Either `--topic-name <registry topic>`, which takes the anchor controls and
the owning team from config/topics.yaml, or `--topic` plus
`--nist-controls` for a one-off topic that isn't in the registry.
synthesize.name: synthesize

params.help: Name of a topic in the registry (config/topics.yaml). Takes its anchor controls and owning team from there, and records the owner in the output so `generate` names the real team instead of [Responsible Team].

wiki-drift.help:
Which published pages changed on the wiki since this tool wrote them.

The question a policy owner asks before a review cycle. `publish` answers
it too, but only as the reason it refused to write, which is the wrong
moment to find out. This writes nothing and prints the `pull` command
that would bring each edit into the repository as a reviewable diff.

A page whose body already says what the repository says is in sync,
whoever wrote its latest version.
wiki-drift.name: wiki-drift

params.name: content_dir

discover.help:
Propose a topic registry from a space nobody has catalogued.

Most of the grouping is already written down, just not as data: a
governance space names its pages by convention (Access Control Policy,
Access Control Standard) and cites the same controls throughout a related
set. Those signals are exact and free, and they place the majority of a
real space with no model involved. The LLM is used only for the residue.

Every proposed owner is [UNASSIGNED]. Nothing in a page reliably says
which team is accountable for it, and a wrong owner in a compliance
artifact is worse than a blank one.
discover.name: discover

params.help: Confluence space key to crawl.
params.name: space

params.help: Confluence base URL. Defaults to `zardoz.host`.
params.name: host

params.help: Where to write the proposal. Deliberately not topics.yaml - it needs owners set before it is usable.
params.name: out

params.help: Refuse to crawl a space larger than this rather than proposing a registry from an arbitrary subset of it.
params.name: max_results

params.help: Group only by naming convention and control citations. Pages no convention reaches are listed rather than clustered.
params.name: no_llm

sync.help:
Build the local snapshot Zardoz answers from.

Reads a markdown content tree, a Confluence space, or both. Markdown
needs no credentials at all, so a repo-backed document set can be synced
and questioned offline. Where both are configured the tree wins: in that
arrangement the file is the source of truth and the page is a copy of it.

Documents that know their owner - from the topic registry, or from their
own frontmatter - are trusted; everything else is supporting context that
answers may use and will say they used.
sync.name: sync

params.help: Markdown content tree to read. Defaults to `zardoz.content_dir` in config.yaml. Needs no credentials.
params.name: content_dir

params.help: Confluence base URL. Defaults to `zardoz.host` in config.yaml. Omit to sync from markdown only.
params.name: host

params.help: Extra space to pull as unowned supporting context. Defaults to `zardoz.supporting_space` in config.yaml. Omit for registry pages only.
params.name: supporting_space

params.help: Refuse to walk a supporting space larger than this, rather than silently syncing an arbitrary subset of it.
params.name: max_results

params.help: Let a sync that resolves nothing clear the existing corpus. Without this, a run that finds no documents leaves the previous snapshot alone.
params.name: allow_empty

zardoz.help:
Ask questions about your published policy set, conversationally.

Run with no subcommand to open the shell. Zardoz reads; it does not
write. It can draft a `policyforge edit-topic` command for you to run,
but every change to a live page still goes through that command's gates.
zardoz.name: zardoz

params.help: Topic registry to load, for ownership and page lookups.
params.name: topics_path

params.help: Where the synced document snapshot lives.
params.name: corpus_dir

params.help: Skip the floating head on launch.
params.name: no_art

params.help: Drop the Zardoz voice from the shell chrome entirely. Answers are plain either way - this only affects greetings, prompts and errors.
params.name: plain
